slides.texte_overlay:
How to feel relaxed on a
first date instead of nervous
Move your body before you go. A short run or a walk an hour before the date burns off the nervous energy. You'll arrive looking relaxed instead of tense and jumpy.
Lower the stakes in your head. It's not an audition, it's two people seeing if they enjoy each other's company. If it's not a match, that's information, not failure.
Prepare three curious questions. "What's something you're excited about lately?" Having a few good questions ready means you never panic when the conversation slows.
Focus on her, not on how you're doing. Nerves come from watching yourself. Get curious about her stories and you'll forget to be nervous within the first ten minutes.
Laugh at the small mishaps. Spilled drink, wrong table, sudden rain. Laughing it off together breaks the tension faster than any perfect line ever could, and it shows you're easy to be around.
Before: overthinking every silence. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and always a fun little story to share when the conversation needs one.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: overthinking every silence. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Now I always have a fun story to share.

slides.texte_overlay: Keep the first date short. An hour or two, then leave on a high note. Short dates feel lighter, and ending while you're both having fun makes a second date easy to plan.
